question.problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}-p+7q=-4 \\ 10p-9q=-21\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

The variable $p$ can be eliminated from the system using the following two steps:

1\. Multiply the first equation by $10$ and obtain

  $$
  \begin{aligned}-10p+70q & =-40.\end{aligned}
  $$

2\. Add the multiplied equation to the second equation to get

$\,$
{{field-1}}
$=-61.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's follow the steps provided:

**Step 1**: Multiplying the first equation by $10$ yields the following equivalent system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}(\,-p+7q=-4\,)\,\times (10) \\ 10p-9q=-21\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}-10p+70q=-40 \\ 10p-9q=-21\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Next, we add these two equations together:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\cancel{10p}+70q & =-40 \\ \cancel{10p}-9q & =-21 \\ (70q-9q) & =(-40-21) \\ 61q & =-61\end{aligned}
$$
